title: Approval is not execution: APPROVED does not mean the external side effect already happened
risk: The UI marks the campaign as done when the decision is registered, so an operator stops watching a job that later fails in the adapter and the customer never receives the message.
preconditions: Namespace gov-apv-<case_id>-<worker_id>; approval queue seeded from fixtures/offline/governance.json.
Operator identities and roles resolved from the fixture operator registry; every decision goes through POST /api/v1/approvals/{id}/decision, the only approval route.
The mock EMAIL adapter is scripted to fail the first dispatch attempt with 503 and succeed on retry.

steps.action: Submit APPROVE and observe the immediate response
steps.expected: The response status is APPROVED with a task id; it does not claim the message was delivered.

steps.action: Observe the first dispatch attempt failing
steps.expected: The execution record shows failed with the upstream 503 preserved; the run is not marked completed.

steps.action: Let the retry run with the same effect_key
steps.expected: The retry succeeds and exactly one external send is recorded with one receipt.

steps.action: Read the run and task records at each stage
steps.expected: Distinct states are visible: approval APPROVED, execution failed then succeeded, task completed only after the receipt.

assertions: Approval status and execution status are different fields and disagree while the job is failing.
A 503 is never reported to the operator as a successful send.
The retry reuses the effect_key, so the eventual delivery is single, not duplicated.
The task only reaches completed after a verified receipt exists.
forbidden: Setting task status completed when the decision is registered.
Reporting success on the queue acknowledgement rather than the provider response.
Creating a second external send on retry.
evidence: Decision response, execution records for both attempts, and the final receipt.
Adapter log with the 503 and the later 200 plus the single effect_key.
cleanup: Delete gov- task and execution rows; the single simulated send is reported as non-recallable.
automation: Real approval-to-execution handoff and retry logic under test; the adapter is the substituted boundary and its script makes the failure deterministic.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
